title: 5th Sitting of Third session of 2026
summary: The 5th sitting of the Third session of 2026 opened with the Deputy Speaker presiding, passed the minutes of the previous sitting with no amendments, and spent the rest of the time debating the government's bill to amend the Criminal Procedure Act (2016/12), sponsored by Funadhoo's Mohamed Mamdooh. The changes give courts more powers to keep secret evidence, informants and investigation methods confidential, and members argued over witness protection, judicial independence and political motives. The bill was accepted for consideration by 45 votes to none and sent to the Judiciary Committee; the next sitting is on 14 October 2026.

items.title: Opening of the sitting and prayer
Announcement of attendance
items.outcome: 26 members present, 8 on leave, 3 on official travel announced

items.title: Passing of the minutes (sitting 28 of the Second session of 2026)
Unfinished business: debate on the government bill to amend the Criminal Procedure Act (2016/12)
items.outcome: debated by 13 members; debate closed when the remaining members who had asked to speak were not in the chamber

items.title: Vote on accepting the Criminal Procedure Act amendment bill for consideration
items.outcome: passed 45-0; referred to the Judiciary Committee

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Supports the amendments, saying the judiciary is not yet fully independent and the Judicial Service Commission's make-up should change.
Defended the removal of the two Supreme Court judges and said the Majlis must be able to make laws.
After the prayer break, explained how sections 131 to 134 limit disclosure of evidence and protect witnesses.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Backs the amendments to evidence and witness rules but says courts and state powers must respect fair-trial rights.
Raised the use of intelligence reports as evidence, saying committee should look at it closely.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Fully supports the amendments, saying they protect witnesses and strengthen investigators.
Argued the criminal justice system needs reform and that past governments left cases unresolved.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Supports the bill, describing how the Criminal Procedure Act has changed over time and what the new amendments add.
Said keeping investigation secrets and witnesses safe is important while courts keep the power to order disclosure.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said large cases often collapse in court and that investigative bodies and the justice system need better coordination.
Supports the amendments as part of improving justice and the government's aim of fairness.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Opposed the bill, linking it to the recent removal of two Supreme Court judges and the role of the Judicial Service Commission.
Argued secret evidence could be used against people, including businesspeople, ahead of the 2028 election, and urged members to reconsider.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Said the bill touches on Islamic Sharia rules about who may give testimony and how it is taken.
Argued that laws made by the Majlis must not conflict with Islam and that witnesses need protection.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said the benefit of the amendments depends on an independent judiciary free of political influence.
Questioned the government's record on the Judicial Service Commission and the removal of two Supreme Court judges.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said laws must apply to everyone and that state money belongs to the public, so wrongdoing needs real consequences.
Responded to earlier members' criticism, arguing the bill is not aimed at any individual.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Welcomed some parts of the bill but warned the changes to section 131 could be used for political ends.
Asked that the committee review the court's power to withhold or reveal evidence.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Rejected the claim that the amendment conflicts with Article 42 of the Constitution.
Said the main problem in the justice system is how laws are applied, and supports the bill going to committee.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Supports the amendment, saying people who report crime need protection and incentives such as insurance.
Said illegitimate wealth should be treated differently from honestly earned wealth, and the law must be enforced.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: As sponsor, said many members had spoken and he hopes the committee reaches a balanced result with other institutions' input.
Linked the bill to Article 40 of the Constitution on property gained through crime, and asked for quick committee passage.

decisions: Minutes of sitting 28 of the Second session of 2026 passed with no amendments.
Bill to amend the Criminal Procedure Act accepted for consideration, 45-0.
Bill sent to the Judiciary Committee for study under rule 106(r) of the Majlis rules.
Next sitting set for 14 October 2026 at 9:00 am.

votes.what: Accept the government's Criminal Procedure Act amendment bill for consideration (23 votes needed; 93 members, 46 present)
